title: Partition Array Into Three Equal Sums
statement:
You are given an array `a` of `n` integers. Choose two indices `i < j` and use them as **partition points**. The elements at the partition points are *excluded* from every sum, so the array splits into three segments:

- the left segment `a[0..i-1]`,
- the middle segment `a[i+1..j-1]`,
- the right segment `a[j+1..n-1]`.

Every segment must contain at least one element. Decide whether some choice of `i` and `j` makes the three segment sums equal.

Print `true` if such a pair of partition points exists, otherwise `false`. Elements may be negative or zero, and the two partition elements can have any values.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers `a[0] ... a[n-1]`.

examples.explanation: Choose the partition points at index 1 (value 9) and index 4 (value 5). The segments are [3], [1, 2] and [3], each with sum 3.

The total is 10. After removing two elements the rest must split into three equal sums, so the remaining total must be divisible by 3; only removing two 2s works (remaining 6, so each segment sums to 2). But every non-empty prefix has sum 1, 3, 4, 6, ..., never 2, so the left segment can never match.
Partition at the two 7s. The segments are [0], [0] and [0], all with sum 0.

hints: Write the three segment sums with prefix sums P: the left sum is P[i], the middle is P[j] - P[i+1], the right is total - P[j+1]. All three must be equal to the same value R.
Fix j and compute R = total - P[j+1] from the right segment. Then you need some earlier i (with i + 2 <= j) such that P[i] = R and P[i+1] = P[j] - R.
Sweep j from left to right and store the pairs (P[i], P[i+1]) of every valid i in a hash set, so each j is answered in O(1). Negative values rule out two pointers.
